description.text: We created Chime to help everyday people make progress in their financial lives. For too long, millions of Americans, including the nearly 75% of the adult population that earn up to $100,000 annually, have struggled with bank relationships that are not always aligned with their best interests. So we set out to create a new approach, built on a foundation of trust rather than fine print and punitive fees. Through our direct relationships with FDIC-insured bank partners, we deliver easy-to-use products that address the most critical financial needs of everyday people — spending, saving, accessing liquidity, and building credit, all while avoiding punitive fees. Since our founding, we are proud to have created some of the most impactful product innovations in consumer banking and payments. Through our broad suite of products, we have built trusted relationships with 9.5 million Active Members, with the majority of them relying on Chime to serve as their primary financial relationship as of December 31, 2025. Being the primary account relationship for our members establishes Chime as their central financial hub, and we believe these relationships are the most valuable in consumer financial services. As the central hub, Chime becomes the platform through which members consistently deposit their paychecks and conduct their everyday spend, creating durable and long-lasting relationships with high engagement.

about.description_short: Chime (Nasdaq: CHYM) is a financial technology company founded on the premise that core banking services should be helpful, easy, and free. We offer a broad range of low-cost banking and payments products that address the most critical financial needs of everyday people. Our member-aligned business model has helped millions of people to unlock financial progress. Member deposits are FDIC-insured through The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A., Members FDIC, up to applicable limits.

analysis_md:
# CHYM — Chime Financial, Inc.
v5.4 run, 2026-10-18. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
US neobank for mass-market / underbanked consumers (founded 2012, IPO June 2025 at $27): free checking/savings, early direct deposit, MyPay earned-wage access and Instant Loans, delivered through partner banks (Stride Bank, The Bancorp Bank) — Chime itself held no charter in the filing period. Revenue is primarily debit interchange (payments revenue $430M of $670M in Q2 2026) earned at the Durbin small-issuer exemption rate via those sub-$10B-asset partners, plus platform-related revenue ($240M in Q2 2026, +48% YoY). 10.4M active members at Q2 2026 (+20% YoY), average revenue per active member $260. Price $29.67 (nasdaq_quote_api); engine market-cap estimate $7.01B on the FY2025 weighted diluted count — the TTM diluted count is 396,943,274, so the live market cap is higher (press put it at ~$11.4B in October 2026); in scope under $40B either way.

## Owner's earnings
**Filed history (financials_history.csv):**
- FY2023: OCF −$156,594,000; SBC $26,035,000; capex $10,501,000 → conservative OE −$193,130,000 = **−$3.06/share**
- FY2024: OCF $64,140,000; SBC $29,845,000; capex $4,812,000 → conservative OE $29,483,000 = **+$0.45/share**
- FY2025: OCF $52,780,000; SBC $1,070,898,000; capex $19,887,000 → conservative OE −$1,038,005,000 = **−$4.39/share**
- Maintenance version FY2025 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): −$1,327,135,000 — worse than the conservative figure, so the conservative OCF-based series is the cleaner one.
- OE positive in only 1 of the last 3 fiscal years. The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is **−$3.06/share** — on the median alone this is Tier F, sub-type no_cash_generation.
- FY2025's collapse is one identifiable item, not operations: the company reports the FY2025 net loss of $1,009,936,000 was primarily driven by $928M of stock-based compensation expense and related payroll tax in Q2 2025, significantly elevated due to the IPO (RSUs whose liquidity condition was satisfied at the IPO, expensed in a catch-up). SBC is a real cost in this system and is NOT added back — but the FY2025 SBC print is a multi-year catch-up in a single year, which is why neither the latest FY nor the median is a usable run-rate base.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $52,780,000 − prior YTD $2,743,000 + current YTD $294,956,000 = **TTM $344,993,000**
- SBC: FY $1,070,898,000 − prior YTD $918,843,000 + current YTD $130,052,000 = **TTM $282,107,000** (the subtraction removes the Q2 2025 IPO catch-up that sits in the prior-YTD leg; the current-YTD leg is the post-IPO run rate)
- Capex: FY $19,887,000 − prior YTD $3,631,000 + current YTD $16,560,000 = **TTM $32,816,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **396,943,274**
- **TTM OE total $30,070,000 → base OE/share $0.0758** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Even on this cleanest, most current base, OE yield at $29.67 is 0.26% — the entire valuation rests on growth and on SBC continuing to fall as a share of OCF. TTM revenue $2,457,032,000 (+26.4% YoY, fundamentals.json), TTM gross margin 88.7%, TTM net income −$18,193,000 despite two consecutive GAAP-profitable quarters in H1 2026 (Q2 net income $27.9M per the Q2 release).

**Balance sheet (FY2025, from the filing via financials_history.csv / fundamentals.json):** cash $466,252,000, restricted cash $14,508,000, short-term investments (marketable securities) $587,828,000, total assets $1,964,605,000, total liabilities $562,899,000, equity $1,401,706,000, lease liabilities $134,665,000. No debt tags report in any year — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK below.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate
Justification: a real brand and primary-account direct-deposit base in an underserved segment, with an owned processing stack, but the core economics rent a regulatory exemption (Durbin small-issuer interchange) through partner banks Chime did not own in the filing period, consumer switching costs are low, and there is no through-cycle record of returns on capital.
- FOR: 10.4M active members with primary-account direct-deposit relationships — the paycheck anchor is the stickiest position in mass-market consumer finance; highest engagement in the category (members transact far more frequently than Cash App peers, per Q2 reporting); ChimeCore owned processing stack — migration completed Q4 2025, company-estimated ~60% lower transaction processing cost, supporting the gross-margin record below; brand leadership in the underbanked segment.
- AGAINST: ~two-thirds of revenue is interchange priced off the Durbin small-bank exemption — a regulatory loophole, not an owned asset; any Durbin expansion or BaaS tightening hits the core directly; no bank charter of its own in the filing period (deposits and issuance sit with Stride / Bancorp); low consumer switching costs vs Cash App, SoFi, Dave, Current and the incumbent banks; member base (household income roughly $35–75K) is the most employment- and spend-cyclical segment; lending expansion (MyPay, Instant Loans) imports credit risk the model has not carried through a downturn.
- Evidence: gross margin 82.8% (FY2023) → 87.6% (FY2024) → 88.0% (FY2025) → 88.7% TTM — high and rising, consistent with an asset-light cost advantage. The `roic_proxy` series in fundamentals.json (8.5% FY2023, 2.2% FY2024, −87.8% FY2025) is NOT meaningful evidence either way: invested capital was negative through the pre-IPO years (equity −$1,953,613,000 in FY2023, −$1,930,600,000 in FY2024, with preferred stock outside equity) and the FY2025 figure is the IPO SBC catch-up flowing through operating income. There is no clean year of ROIC above the cost of capital on the record — that absence, not the distorted series, is why the moat cannot score higher.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended start is 25.76% (revenue CAGRs 30.76% / 30.76%, latest YoY +30.69%, all reduced 5pp for the share-count adjustment — see DILUTION). Against actual prints: FY2025 revenue +30.7%, Q2 2026 revenue +27% YoY, FY2026 company guidance $2.725–2.745B (+25–26%) — the base start of 25.8% sits right on the guided print, no recalibration needed. Bull (30.8%) matches the FY2023–25 revenue CAGR. Super bull (37.8%) is above every recent consolidated print and is justified only as the low-probability case where platform-related revenue (FY2025 +73%, Q2 2026 +48%) becomes the dominant mix — it carries the default 10% weight and nothing more. Default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp), default OE multipliers (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) and default probabilities (10/25/30/25/10) are retained: the uncertainty here is the OE base (0.26% yield), not the growth path, and the multipliers already span it. Price $29.67.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | 13.8% | 0.75 | Durbin/BaaS tightening or a consumer downturn hits interchange; SBC stays heavy | $0.71 | 2.84% (at floor) |
| Bear | 25% | 20.8% | 0.90 | Growth decays to the low-20s; SBC run rate sticky | $1.11 | 3.05% |
| Base | 30% | 25.8% | 1.00 | Guided growth; TTM OE base compounds from $0.0758 | $1.47 | 3.25% |
| Bull | 25% | 30.8% | 1.10 | FY23–25 CAGR holds; platform mix lifts OE conversion | $1.94 | 3.51% |
| Super bull | 10% | 37.8% | 1.25 | Platform revenue becomes dominant; SBC leverage compounds | $2.80 | 4.00% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $1.55 (−94.8% vs price), IV@12% $2.14, IV@10% $2.80, weighted IRR 3.30%, base-case IRR 3.25%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear and bull both D — no TIER_BAND). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 0.26%, terminal value 22.2% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.93x, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices: $1.55 clears 15%, $1.04 clears 20%, $0.76 clears 25% — the stock would need to fall ~95% for this OE base to clear Andrew's 15% hurdle.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended ~10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **DILUTION** (share count +93.4%/yr): an IPO artifact, not an ongoing run rate — diluted weighted shares went 63,104,219 (FY2023) → 64,910,056 (FY2024) → 236,270,347 (FY2025) → 396,943,274 (TTM YTD) as preferred stock converted and IPO RSUs entered the count. The engine's −5pp growth adjustment is retained as conservative. The real ongoing dilution is SBC: $26,035,000 (FY2023) → $29,845,000 (FY2024) → $1,070,898,000 (FY2025, IPO catch-up) → $130,052,000 in H1 2026 alone; TTM SBC $282,107,000 consumes 82% of TTM OCF — that, not the conversion mechanics, is the dilution that matters, and it is fully deducted in the OE base. Fundamentals also show TTM buybacks of $299,612,000 against issuance of $38,023,000, a partial offset.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025): identified — the non-cash SBC add-back. FY2025 net income −$1,009,936,000 vs OCF +$52,780,000 is the $1,070,898,000 SBC (dominated by the $928M IPO catch-up per the company's release) plus working-capital moves (ΔNWC +$327,312,000 in the history file). FY2024 net income −$25,344,000 vs OCF +$64,140,000 is the same mechanism at normal scale (SBC $29,845,000). The OCF-based conservative OE deducts SBC in full, so the divergence does not flatter the base.
- **THIN_HISTORY** (only 3 fiscal years): real — FY2023 is the first filed year in the EDGAR history used here and the company has been public only since June 2025. No through-cycle evidence exists; confidence is capped accordingly.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest FY — net debt UNKNOWN, not zero): stated from the filing — the balance sheet above shows cash $466,252,000 plus marketable securities $587,828,000 against total liabilities of $562,899,000 (largely operating / member-related and accrued items, plus lease liabilities $134,665,000) and no borrowings reported under any debt tag in any filed year. This is a net-cash, unlevered balance sheet; the engine simply cannot compute a net-debt figure from blank tags, so none is quoted.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted — an interchange-funded neobank's cash generation is not capex-cycle OE in the industrial sense, member balances sit with partner banks, and the pending Stride acquisition changes the model itself. Confidence is **low** per the rule, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **IRR_AT_FLOOR** (super-bear IRR within 0.5pp of the 2.5% terminal growth): the super-bear IRR reads "at most ~3%" — at $29.67 against a $0.0758 base, the price is beyond the model's expressive range in every scenario (even super bull returns only 4.00%). The weighted 3.30% should be read as "approximately zero real compensation for the risk," not as a precise return estimate.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (base OE yield 0.3%): real and decisive — the valuation rests almost entirely on growth and SBC normalization. Even granting the bull growth path for 15 years, IV@15% reaches only $1.94.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The method range is the story: on the 3-yr median base (−$3.06/share) the name is an unscoreable Tier F; on the cleanest current base (TTM, IPO SBC catch-up removed by the TTM subtraction itself) it is a Tier D with a weighted IV@15% of $1.55 — 5% of the price. No defensible OE method gets anywhere near $29.67; the market price is a bet on adjusted-EBITDA-style earnings (FY2026 Adj. EBITDA guided to $465–475M) that treat ~$260M+/yr of ongoing SBC as free. In this system SBC is a real cost, and on that basis Chime currently converts $2.46B of TTM revenue into $30.07M of owner's earnings.
- The operating business is genuinely improving — revenue +27% in Q2 2026, gross margin 88.7% TTM, second consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter, guidance raised, platform revenue +48% — and none of it closes a 95% valuation gap on OE math. Improvement would have to show up as OCF growing much faster than the SBC run rate for several years before a re-run could move this.
- Post-filing event (after the FY2025 10-K, before this run): on September 8, 2026 Chime agreed to acquire its partner Stride Bank for $590M cash, expected to close H1 2027 pending OCC approval — roughly 56% of its cash + marketable securities at FY2025. Owning the charter internalizes partner-bank economics (company-estimated >$100M net synergies) but adds bank capital/liquidity requirements and a hard strategic constraint: preserving the Durbin small-issuer exemption means keeping the combined bank under $10B of assets (combined assets already ~$7B per analyst estimates), which caps the deposit growth the model depends on. Not in any filed number used here; a re-run after close will need the new balance sheet. Also announced after Q2 2026: a ~10% workforce reduction (August 2026) — cost action that supports the SBC/opex normalization story but is not yet in filed figures.
- Insider sales of ~$75M in the days after the Q2 beat (largely under 10b5-1 plans, plus a pre-IPO backer sale) are noted, not weighted — they do not change the OE arithmetic.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 3.30% on the TTM base; Tier F on the normalized median base — sized to the conservative end, D is the generous reading)
- Confidence: **Low** (SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH, thin 3-year history, 0.26% OE yield, IRR at the model floor in the bear cases)
- One-liner: Fast-growing neobank with an 89% gross margin but almost no owner's earnings after real SBC — moat 4/10, weighted IRR 3.3%, IV@15% $1.55 vs $29.67; does not clear 15% until ~$1.55.
